implementation: Application-owned signed 16-bit interleaved PCM, voice DSP and native OS audio boundary. Handwritten ctypes bindings and stdlib algorithms; no PortAudio, sounddevice or NumPy runtime payload or global compatibility namespace.
consumer_selection: The verified bundle selects hermes_platform.audio.native_audio_io through the original lazy voice and TTS import boundaries. Source installations retain their SDK/PM branch. The original macOS output permission policy still routes voice/TTS playback through afplay.
checks: Independent NumPy 1.26.4 oracle PCM vectors cover beeps, thinking cues, mono/stereo warmup, RMS and percentile interpolation. Committed tests decode ordinary JSON bytes using stdlib only; waveform rounding tolerance is one signed-16 sample unit.

Controlled native-device boundary exercises actual callback/manual streams, background playback, cancellation, overflow and error propagation, close/drain lifetimes and no device open on construction.
Portable fixed-width WinMM, PulseAudio and AudioQueue ABI tests execute native callback and buffer handling without pretending to run another host OS.
Linux native ALSA null PCM capture/output uses an explicit private ALSA configuration and never the default microphone or speakers.
The actual PulseAudio client library is tested against an explicitly absent private Unix socket, proving bounded native connection errors without consulting a user audio server.

An isolated original bundled consumer fixture calls the real _import_audio, AudioRecorder, WAV playback, both barge-in listeners and streaming TTS; only the OS device provider is controlled. NumPy, sounddevice, subprocesses and network audio services are absent.
evidence_limits: Successful PulseAudio/PipeWire service I/O and physical Linux microphone/speaker behavior are not claimed: no private Pulse server executable or authorized physical-device test is available on this host.
Windows winMM and macOS AudioQueue/CoreAudio have portable ABI/lifecycle fixtures, but real host capture/playback remains unverified. Native enumeration tests run only on their actual host.

The consumed voice/TTS device format is signed 16-bit PCM, normally mono with stereo WAV playback. Unsupported native formats, unavailable OS libraries, device permission failures and capture overflow raise explicit errors.
Local neural inference, wake-word engines and compressed-audio file synthesis are separate native dependencies; these PCM and OS audio adapters do not emulate their models or claim their validation.
